title: Kentucky Paycheck Calculator 2026 – Take-Home Pay
description: Calculate your Kentucky take-home pay after federal taxes, Kentucky's 3.5% income tax, local occupational taxes, Social Security and Medicare.
heading: Kentucky Paycheck Calculator

parts.markdown:
Use our free **Kentucky paycheck calculator** to estimate your take-home pay after federal income tax, Kentucky state income tax, Social Security, Medicare and applicable local occupational taxes.

Enter your annual salary or hourly wage, select your payment frequency and customize your payroll deductions to understand how much money you could receive on payday.

Kentucky reduced its state income tax rate to 3.5% in 2026. However, employees working in certain cities and counties may also pay local occupational taxes, making employment location an important part of calculating take-home income.

Whether you work in Louisville, Lexington, Bowling Green, Covington or another Kentucky community, understanding your net earnings can help you compare job offers and manage household expenses.

## How to Use the Kentucky Paycheck Calculator

Begin by selecting the type of compensation you receive.

Salaried employees should enter their annual gross income, while hourly employees should provide their hourly wage, regular working hours and qualifying overtime hours.

Next, select your payment frequency. Enter federal and Kentucky income tax withheld for the pay period from your pay stub.

If your employment is subject to local occupational taxes, enter the total amount withheld for the pay period.

Include retirement contributions, healthcare premiums and other employee deductions.

Review your estimated gross pay, individual tax deductions and remaining take-home income.

For greater accuracy, use the information from your latest payroll statement rather than estimating your deductions.

## Kentucky Payroll Taxes in 2026

Kentucky employees generally encounter several categories of payroll deductions.

Kentucky's annual standard deduction for 2026 is $3,360.

The amount deducted from your paycheck depends on taxable earnings, payment frequency, local tax requirements, withholding elections and employee benefits.

Visit the [Kentucky Department of Revenue](https://revenue.ky.gov/Business/Pages/Employer-Payroll-Withholding.aspx) for official employer withholding guidance.

## How Kentucky State Income Tax Works

Kentucky uses a flat individual income tax rate.

For 2026, the applicable state income tax withholding rate is 3.5%, down from 4% in 2025.

Unlike progressive tax systems, Kentucky does not use increasingly higher individual income tax rates as taxable earnings rise.

However, multiplying your entire gross salary by 3.5% may overestimate your ordinary state withholding because the calculation accounts for the applicable standard deduction.

Employees receiving multiple paychecks during the year have the standard deduction distributed across their regular payroll periods.

The amount withheld throughout the year may differ from the final tax liability calculated on your annual income tax return.

Review the [Kentucky standard deduction announcement](https://revenue.ky.gov/News/Pages/Kentucky-DOR-Announces-2026-Standard-Deduction.aspx) for the official annual amount.

## How to Calculate Kentucky Income Tax Withholding

Suppose an employee earns $65,000 annually and receives 26 biweekly paychecks.

The gross biweekly paycheck is $2,500.

First, determine annualized earnings:

$2,500 × 26 = $65,000

Subtract the annual Kentucky standard deduction:

$65,000 − $3,360 = $61,640

Apply the state withholding rate:

$61,640 × 3.5% = $2,157.40

Divide by the number of annual pay periods:

$2,157.40 ÷ 26 = approximately $82.98

Under these assumptions, the employee's estimated Kentucky income tax withholding is $82.98 per paycheck.

This example assumes ordinary regular wages, no withholding exemption and no additional requested withholding.

The official [2026 Kentucky withholding formula](https://revenue.ky.gov/Forms/2026%20Withholding%20Formula.pdf) explains the calculation methodology.

## Understanding Kentucky Form K-4

Kentucky employees use Form K-4 to provide applicable state withholding information.

The form allows qualifying employees to claim exemption from withholding or request additional withholding.

Unlike certain other states, Kentucky's ordinary withholding calculation does not use a system of personal withholding exemptions for each dependent.

Employees may qualify for special withholding treatment under certain circumstances, including eligible interstate employment arrangements and military-related exemptions.

However, claiming exemption from withholding requires meeting specific eligibility requirements.

Download the official [2026 Kentucky withholding certificate](https://revenue.ky.gov/Forms/42A804%20%28K-4%29%20%282026%29.pdf) for further information.

## Kentucky Local Occupational Taxes

One important feature of Kentucky payroll is the presence of occupational taxes imposed by certain local governments.

Depending on your employment location, you may encounter city, county or other local occupational taxes.

These deductions are separate from Kentucky state income tax.

Local taxable wage definitions may also differ from state or federal income-taxable wages.

As a result, a deduction that reduces your federal taxable income may not necessarily reduce your local occupational tax by the same amount.

Employees working remotely or performing duties in multiple jurisdictions may need to allocate their earnings according to the applicable local requirements.

Consult the relevant local tax authority to confirm the applicable occupational tax rate.

## Louisville Paycheck Calculator: Local Occupational Tax

Louisville Metro imposes occupational taxes on applicable employee compensation.

The published ordinary rates are:

parts.caption: Louisville Paycheck Calculator: Local Occupational Tax

parts.markdown:
Consider an employee receiving $2,500 in earnings fully subject to Louisville occupational tax.

For a qualifying resident employee:

$2,500 × 2.20% = $55.00

For a qualifying nonresident employee:

$2,500 × 1.45% = $36.25

The difference is $18.75 per paycheck under these assumptions.

Employees performing some of their work outside Louisville Metro may require additional adjustments.

Consult the [Louisville Metro Revenue Commission](https://louisvilleky.gov/government/revenue-commission) for official occupational tax requirements.

Do not apply Louisville's rates to every Kentucky city or county.

## Federal Payroll Taxes for Kentucky Employees

Federal income tax withholding is calculated separately using the employee's taxable earnings and Form W-4 information.

In 2026, employees generally contribute 6.2% of covered Social Security wages, subject to an annual taxable wage limit of $184,500.

Ordinary Medicare withholding applies at 1.45% of covered earnings without a standard annual wage ceiling.

Employers generally withhold an additional 0.9% on Medicare-covered wages exceeding $200,000 paid by that employer during the calendar year.

Employees with more than one employer may have additional considerations when calculating annual tax liability.

Review [IRS Publication 15](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15) and [Publication 15-T](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15t) for official federal payroll guidance.

## Kentucky Paycheck Example: $65,000 Annual Salary

Consider a Louisville resident earning $65,000 annually and receiving $2,500 biweekly.

Assume the employee is subject to ordinary Kentucky withholding, Louisville resident occupational tax and federal payroll contributions, with no applicable annual contribution limits reached.

Approximately $2,170.77 remains before federal income tax withholding and other employee deductions.

An employee earning the same salary in a location without an applicable occupational tax would have approximately $55 more remaining under otherwise identical assumptions.

This example illustrates selected payroll deductions rather than a complete net paycheck.

Enter your actual federal withholding and employee benefit information into the calculator to obtain your estimated take-home pay.

## Kentucky Hourly Paycheck Calculator

Hourly employees can estimate their gross earnings using regular working hours and qualifying overtime.

Suppose a Kentucky employee earns $25 per hour and works 40 regular hours plus eight qualifying overtime hours paid at time-and-a-half.

Regular earnings:

$25 × 40 = $1,000

Overtime earnings:

$25 × 1.5 × 8 = $300

Total gross earnings:

$1,300

Applicable federal income tax, Kentucky withholding, local occupational taxes and employee contributions are then calculated using their respective taxable wage amounts.

Employees working in manufacturing, logistics, healthcare and hospitality may receive variable earnings because of shift differentials or overtime.

Review the [US Department of Labor overtime guidance](https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/overtime) before estimating compensation for employment arrangements involving exemptions or specialized schedules.

## Working Across Kentucky State Borders

Kentucky has reciprocal income tax arrangements with Illinois, Indiana, Michigan, Ohio, Virginia, West Virginia and Wisconsin.

These agreements can affect the state income tax treatment of qualifying compensation earned by interstate workers.

However, special conditions apply to certain arrangements. Virginia's agreement generally requires daily commuting, while Ohio's agreement has restrictions involving certain shareholder-employees.

State income tax reciprocity does not automatically eliminate local occupational taxes.

Employees should confirm eligibility and provide the appropriate withholding certificate before claiming an exemption.

## Managing Your Kentucky Take-Home Income

Use estimated net income rather than gross salary when establishing your household budget.

Compare housing costs, commuting expenses, insurance premiums and employer retirement contributions alongside paycheck deductions.

Employees with multiple jobs should review their Kentucky withholding because more than one employer may account for the standard deduction independently.

Our [emergency fund calculator](/savings/emergency-fund-calculator/) can help you establish a suitable savings target, while our [salary-to-hourly calculator](/calculators/salary-to-hourly-calculator/) can help compare different compensation arrangements.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is Kentucky's income tax rate in 2026?

Kentucky applies a flat individual income tax withholding rate of 3.5%. The applicable annual standard deduction is $3,360.

### Does Louisville have a separate employee occupational tax?

Yes. Louisville Metro publishes ordinary occupational tax rates of 2.2% for qualifying resident employees and 1.45% for qualifying nonresident employees.

### Do all Kentucky employees pay local occupational taxes?

No. Occupational taxes depend on the applicable employment jurisdiction and local rules. Rates and taxable wage definitions can vary between cities and counties.
